(Per: Hon'Ble Mr Justice Sachin Shankar Magadum)

The appeal is by the appellant/claimant assailing the liability fastened on respondent No.1/owner of the offending vehicle on the premises that there is a breach of policy conditions and also compensation awarded by the Tribunal globally at a sum of Rs.25,000.
2.
Heard the counsel on record.
I have also given my anxious consideration to the Trial Court records.

3. In the case on hand, appellant/claimant has filed a claim petition alleging that he has suffered fractures in a road traffic accident dated 18.03.2017 and has claimed compensation alleging that he has suffered permanent disability.

The Tribunal on examination of NC: 2024:KHC-K:8241 medical records produced by the claimant, has proceeded to discard this evidence primarily on the ground that these medical records are dated of July, 2017 while claimant has suffered injuries in a road traffic accident dated 18.03.2017.
The Tribunal further noticed that though appellant/claimant is asserting that he suffered permanent disability, neither doctor is examined nor disability certificate is produced.
In absence of medical evidence, global compensation of Rs.25,000/- is awarded and since there is a breach of policy conditions, Tribunal has fastened liability on the owner of the offending vehicle.
4. Insofar as a global compensation of Rs.25,000/- is concerned, it appears to be on the lower side.

More particularly, when the Trial Court records reveal that claimant has placed on record the wound certificate, which clearly reveals that claimant has suffered fracture of 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th metatarsal of the left foot. The fact that wound certificate reveals that claimants has also suffered fracture of 5th proximal phalanx, an additional sum of NC: 2024:KHC-K:8241 Rs.1,35,000/- is awarded apart from of Rs.25,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

sentences.text:
The finding of the Tribunal fastening liability on owner is perverse and contrary to law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Pappu and Others vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba and Another1 as well as the Full Bench judgment of this Court in the case of New India Assurance Company Limited vs.
Yallavva and Another2.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Full Bench held that mere breach of policy conditions will not absolve the insurance company from its liability.
Even if there is a breach of policy conditions, the primary liability to satisfy the award lies on the insurance company with liberty to recover it from the owner of the offending vehicle.

6. For the foregoing reasons, this Court passes the following:
ORDER a) Appeal is allowed in part.

(2018) 3 SCC 208 (2020) 3 KCCR 1469 NC:
2024:KHC-K:8241 b) Appellant/claimant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.1,35,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till its realization.
c) Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company shall satisfy the entire compensation amount and recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.
d) The entire amount shall be released in favour of the appellant/claimant on proper identification.
